newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA'S HEALY BANNED FOR DISSENT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA'S HEALY BANNED FOR DISSENT.

text.p: Australian vice-captain Ian Healy was banned for two matches after being found guilty of dissent during the third and final test against South Africa at Centurion Park on Monday.
Healy glowered angrily with hand on hip at umpire Cyril Mitchley after the decision was made and stamped from the field before throwing his bat through the dressing-room door.
He will miss Australia's one-day internationals against South Africa at East London on Friday and Port Elizabeth on Monday.
A replacement wicketkeeper was being flown out from Australia as test reserve Justin Langer had already been told he was not required for the one-day series. His wife is due to give birth this week.
Healy was adjudged caught behind down the legside off the bowling of Brett Schultz for 12. Replays showed the delivery may have glanced off the pad rather than bat.

"Team captain and officials were told at the pre-series meeting earlier in the month that the players must accept the umpires' decisions or face suspensions," said match referee Raman Subba Row of England.
